what_it_does: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is a technique that lets a computer do useful calculations on data that is still encrypted — so a cloud server can process your private data without ever seeing it in the clear. The catch is that FHE is extraordinarily slow: the math involved is roughly 10,000 times heavier than working with unencrypted numbers. A key step called 'bootstrapping' refreshes the encrypted data so computation can continue, but it requires very large number-theoretic transforms (NTT — a way of rearranging number sequences to speed up multiplication) as well as fast Fourier transforms (FFT — the same idea but for ordinary floating-point numbers). ABC-FHE is a chip accelerator designed specifically to speed up the encoding and decoding work the client's device must do before and after sending data to the server. It uses a single reconfigurable math engine that can switch between NTT and FFT modes, generates random numbers and lookup tables on the fly to avoid storing them in off-chip memory, and schedules tasks carefully to keep the hardware busy.
